gist: Pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton has died at the age of 90.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Computer pioneer Margaret Hamilton has died aged 90, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology announced. The Guardian reported she died on 30 September, while Ars Technica noted she died last week. Hamilton learned programming at MIT, worked on weather simulations and air defence projects, and became the first programmer and first woman hired by MIT's Instrumentation Lab for Nasa's Apollo programme. In 2016, President Barack Obama presented her with the nation's highest civilian honour, which the BBC called the Presidential Medal of Honor and other outlets identified as the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hamilton coined the term software engineering and directed the Apollo onboard flight software development. During the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing, her software's failsafe mechanisms compensated for computer overloads, averting an abort and allowing the Eagle module to land safely.

sections.text: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for solving the mystery of life's asymmetry. gist: El Niño is growing and influences weather globally.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A strong El Niño event is developing in the Pacific Ocean and releasing heat into the atmosphere. This climate phenomenon affects weather patterns worldwide and increases the probability of wet and stormy conditions during the UK autumn. In the late winter period, energy from El Niño can travel upwards to disrupt the polar vortex.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: A disrupted polar vortex can raise the probability of cold weather, ice and snow in the UK. Past winters show mixed evidence as some El Niño years brought extreme cold while others remained very warm, and major cold snaps occurred during different climate phases.

sections.heading: What happens next
